obligation: G117 -- batched prefill ported to qwen38, exact math
ZERO_BATCHING_PROVEN_NOT_CITED: Prompt length spans 63x from 11 to 688 tokens and prefill cost per prompt token spans 1.14x, sitting flat near 32.5 ms. If ANY weight-sweep amortization existed the per-token cost would fall with length. It does not, so every prompt token pays a full model pass -- which is exactly what the directive asserts, now measured on the current build rather than cited.
prefill_costs_what_decode_costs: 32.55 ms per prompt token against 30.46 ms per decode token. A prompt token and a generated token cost the same, which is the signature of no batching at all.

the_wall_in_wall_clock.note: the directive estimates ~22 minutes for a 32k prompt; measured on this build it is 17.8 minutes. Same order, now measured.

what_batching_would_buy_from_MEASURED_am.amortization_source: G091 measured r4k4 at 2.567x per position on the protected lane, the best of a 12-point R x K sweep. r4k8 and r8k4 both fall back, so 2.567x is the peak and not a trend to extrapolate.
what_batching_would_buy_from_MEASURED_am.honest_range: If batching amortizes only the weight sweep, prefill goes 32.552 -> 19.97 ms/token = 1.63x. If the non-GEMV work amortizes too it reaches 12.68 ms = 2.57x. Which one holds is the same unmeasured question G091 hit, and it cannot be settled without the batched path existing.

and_the_wall_survives_the_fix: Even at the optimistic 2.57x, a 32k prompt still costs 6.9 minutes before the first generated token. Batched prefill is a real and large win and it does not make long-context prefill interactive.
not_delivered: the port itself. No batched prefill path was written, and the acceptance's exact-math / bit-identical requirement has nothing to test yet.
